Write the README first

Before I write any code for a new service, I write the README. What it does, how you call it, what it will never do. This forces the interface decisions to happen in prose, where they are cheap to change and easy for anyone to review.

Last quarter our team did this for 12 internal services and design review time dropped from about two weeks to three days, because reviewers argued about the README instead of the implementation. Reviewers who never would have opened a pull request left comments on the README.

If you can't explain the interface in one page, the design isn't done. That is the whole rule, and it has held up across every service we have shipped since.
